note: v1: first version of 'Hail on a Music Box' (Tape Weather t4), GLITCHY IDM-LITE, a broken music box in a lo-fi beat. 86 bpm, 58 bars, 162 s, Dbmaj9 | Cm7(11) | Fm9 | Bbm9. THE CLOCKWORK runs dead straight: a toy piano on a 5-sixteenth cycle, a music box on a 7, Ferrous Bloom's crystal on the quarters, realigning only every 140 sixteenths, all through a wobbling (chorus-as-wow), lightly crushed, occasionally stuttering toy bus. Against it the BEAT is played by hand: a tight kit swung at 0.58, the snare dragged late, kick patterns shifting bar by bar, dropped hats and ghost notes, crushed and taped. THE HIDDEN MELODY is a tape lead that sings wherever the toy and the box coincide (124 meeting points), so the gears write the tune. Form: the toys enter one by one over vinyl crackle, the beat arrives soft, the melody appears, a GLITCH break tears the toy into falling 32nd HAIL, the return lifts the melody an octave, a beatless breakdown, full, and an outro where the gears drop out one by one. Mix: the first render had no floor (35-90 Hz 15-25 dB under the album, master rms -19 / crest 17), so a sine sub doubles the roots an octave down, the bass and kick come up, and the master pushes into its ceiling: 83.0 -> 93.04 (master in range, spectrum 34 -> 69, cohesion 31 -> 66; rhythm 100 from the swing). motifs.md and sounds.md rows added.
next: Spectrum 69: the mids are still 5-12 dB proud (bands 13-24) and the top 7-14 dB shy (the lp 6-7k on the drum and toy buses): open the hats' air, tame the pad/toys' mids; listen to the hidden melody's phrasing; Harry's notes when they come.

note: v2: the clockwork CHANGES GEAR, and the song now sits on real tape and vinyl. Songwriting: the gears change ratio by section, so the hidden melody (the tape lead singing where toy and music box meet) changes rhythm with them: in the return the toy piano turns on a 6 against the box's 7, a dotted-eighth hemiola that drags the tune across the bar; in the full section the crystal leaves the quarters for a 9, three odd gears (5, 7, 9) turning at once. Sound, with wM's new lo-fi toolkit: his tape deck is now the wow on the toy bus (warble, flutter, drift, hiss: v1 faked it with a chorus) and on the pad; the master plays back through his tape and vinyl (crackle, dust, rumble, warp, wear) instead of a crackle patch holding one note; the kit is lofi-kit with his wonk (snare nudged 22 ms late, kick 8 ms early, each bar its own swing, a drunk lean) instead of my hand-dragged snare; the drum and toy buses open to 10 kHz and a -3 dB dip at 600 Hz eases the proud mids. Seeds 0/11 (pin 232211dd; v1 byte-identical on it): 93.07 / 93.13 -> 97.89 / 97.90; spectrum 69 -> 98, cohesion 66 -> 99, master rms -12.9 / crest 11.5. motifs.md (THE GEAR CHANGE) and sounds.md updated.
next: Harry's notes when they come; a new section or counter-line (a bass melody answering the hidden melody? a tape-stop into the breakdown?); the intro is 8 bars of toys alone: consider a vinyl-only first bar; rate others' Tape Weather tracks.

note: v3: the song now ENDS the way its title promises: the music box RUNS DOWN. I rewrote the outro as a WIND-DOWN: instead of the gears simply dropping out, every gear's cycle lengthens bar by bar (the toy piano from 5 to 10 sixteenths, the music box from 7 to 17, the crystal from 4 to 9), so the clockwork audibly slows; the pitches sag a semitone every two bars as a mechanism does when its spring gives out; the notes fade; the beat gives out at bar 55; and the last sound is a single music-box note three semitones flat, ringing into the vinyl. And THE BASS now ANSWERS instead of holding roots: the root, a reply on the swung and-of-3 (the fifth, or the ninth up high on alternate chords), then a chromatic walk down into each chord change, so the low end talks back to the hidden melody. Seeds 0/11 (rebaselined: v2 98.12 / 98.11 with the album's flow term): 98.16 / 98.14; cohesion -> 99+. motifs.md: THE WIND-DOWN, THE BASS ANSWERS.
next: Harry's notes when they come; the intro (8 bars of toys alone) could open on a key being wound (a ratchet of rimclicks speeding up) answering the wind-down; a counter-melody for the breakdown; rate t2/t3/t5/t6/t7.
